P1.evidence: P1a partial — the application is acknowledged but not read back: 'I saw your application, but brief me in, like, let's get in details.' Nothing from it is reflected, so the prospect gets no sense of being seen. P1b miss — the four-part frame is never set; the call goes from banter about Poland and Slovakia straight into open discovery. P1c miss — no frame agreement is sought, no 'does that work?'. P1d hit — clean open question: 'What's been going on? What have you tried? And, yeah, how can...' preceded by 'we're here to talk about your fitness, your health, and how can we actually help you with that, yeah?'

P2.evidence: The single worst phase. P2d is the only genuine hit: 'Have some limitations in their movements, in their body? Is there anything that's happening for you? Any injuries or anything like, you know, lower back pains, hips, whatever?' Everything else is either absent or volunteered. P2a miss — age surfaces only from the birthday exchange, height and weight are never asked at all. P2b miss — Erik volunteers 'you sit behind the desk' unprompted; the rep only reflects it back later. P2c miss — health conditions, hereditary history, blood pressure and cardiac history are never asked, on a call that sells loaded ballistic training to a 45-year-old. P2e/P2f miss — the actual current training week and days trained are never established; the rep sells a 3-4x/week programme without knowing what he trains now. P2g miss — Erik volunteers 'I don't have many problems with diet' and 'I don't have any problem with alcohol'; never asked. P2h miss — sleep surfaces only inside Erik's own aside about travel. P2i miss — daily energy never asked, despite energy being the prospect's stated primary goal.

P3.evidence: The strongest work on the call, but reached by improvisation rather than by the script. P3e hit — 'And what does actually feeling better mean to you? Because for me, it can be a different thing than to you, right?' is exactly the scripted move and it is what unlocks the daughter. P3g hit — the rep drives all the way through to family, identity and longevity: the daughter at 15 in the mountains, 'you want to be the kind of granddad, probably in the future, that's not going to be sitting on the couch', grip strength and lifespan. P3b partial — 'what's the biggest reason you want to' substitutes for the mobility/strength/energy menu. P3c partial — the 'something physical you can't do' (keeping up swimming, stairs) emerges from P3e rather than being asked. P3d partial — the explicit 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this' bridge is never said in those terms. P3a miss — the one-thing-you-would-change question is never asked. P3f miss — 'Who else does that impact?' is never asked; Erik volunteers his daughter unprompted, which the script credits to luck, not to the rep. P3h partial — the reflect-back is delivered as a monologue ('when I asked you about feeling better, you mentioned your daughter... you still want to play with her. That's a fact, yeah') rather than as a checked 'so this isn't really about X — is that right?'.

P4.evidence: P4a hit — 'What have you tried?' asked in the opening. P4c hit — the key question of the call: 'why, throughout all those years, why weren't you consistent in training?' P4e hit — Erik names the gap himself in plain terms: 'what is killing me is inconsistency' and then the deeper one, 'sometimes I may have been a little bit cocky, like I don't need it'. P4b partial — the history is narrated at length by the prospect rather than drawn out by a distinct follow-up. P4d partial — 'Why work was more important than playing tennis, for example, just for fun?' gets close to the single blocker but the rep does not land it as 'what's the ONE thing getting in the way'. P4f miss — the 'information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' frame is never delivered, which is the one that would have set up the accountability pillar.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was asserted by the rep and volunteered by the prospect, never elicited. P5a partial — the rep states the consequence instead of asking for it: 'if you won't take care of this now, when she's going to be like, I don't know, 15...' and 'it's going to get worse if you don't do something'. The genuinely powerful version came unprompted from Erik ('I literally am afraid that in five years, I will be 50... I will be completely like useless'), which the script does not credit. P5b miss — 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' never asked. P5c miss — no 'why not?'. P5d miss — no line-in-the-sand question; the nearest thing is the commitment question in P6. Because the prospect handed the rep his own two-year fear for free, the phase looks emotionally complete while none of the four scripted moves were actually run.

P6.evidence: P6a partial — 'So how do you feel in an overall' is a temperature check, not the scripted belief question about structure and the right person in his corner; it does draw out 'I feel good and I like it'. P6b partial — 'If we can figure out all the details, are you really fully committed to showing up and doing the work that needs to be done?' is the right question, but the transcript shows the rep answering himself and moving straight on — 'needs to be done? All right. So look, next steps are pretty easy' — with no recorded YES. P6c partial — the rep advanced to the investment without securing that clear yes. Sequencing note: the three pillars were presented at ~00:24:44, a full thirteen minutes BEFORE the commitment check at ~00:37:36, inverting the script's core instruction to get a genuine verbal yes BEFORE presenting anything.

P11.evidence: P11a partial — the link was sent promptly and twice by different routes, but payment was not collected: 'It's loading, loading, loading, but it doesn't work' / 'I have VPN and I cannot go over it because it's my computer'. The rep correctly refused to let it drift, insisting 'I need to have it on the call because I need to onboard you right after' and booking a same-evening reconvene at 20:30. P11b hit — Trevor's calendar pulled up live and 19:15 the next evening agreed. P11c miss — no agreement or contract is mentioned at any point, let alone signed on the call. P11d miss — no welcome email, no Skool community link, no onboarding questionnaire mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: No think-about-it. The prospect agreed before the rep finished asking.
No spouse consult raised; a partner is never mentioned.
No money objection whatsoever. $6,000 landed with 'We must. Let's do it, man.' No financial picture was taken and none was needed.

Timing was pre-empted by the rep asking for it early — 'what's your time on actually doing something about this, is it months from now or more like' — and the prospect closed it off himself: 'No, no, I can start now... I don't want to prolong this any more.'
No fear or doubt about the modality. The only hesitancy expressed was about his own consistency, which the rep converted into the accountability pillar.

SCRIPT GAP — payment link blocked by the prospect's corporate VPN. There is no scripted play for a technical payment failure at the moment of close. The rep improvised reasonably (re-sent by a second route, diagnosed ad-blocker then VPN, held the line on paying today, booked a 20:30 reconvene) but had no alternative rail to offer — no manual card capture, no invoice, no phone payment — and a fully committed buyer left the call unpaid. This is the second payment-mechanics failure in this batch and it is a systems gap, not a rep failure.

notes: Excellent emotional discovery sitting on top of an almost non-existent baseline. Andrew is genuinely good at P3 and P4 — the daughter-at-15 thread and 'why weren't you consistent' did the whole job — but he skipped eight of nine baseline checks, ran no real consequence frame, presented all three pillars before taking a commitment, and never touched the agreement. Two concrete coaching actions: (1) ask P2c health conditions before selling ballistic loading to any 45-year-old, non-negotiable; (2) take the commitment check before the pillar presentation, not thirteen minutes after it. The close was easy because the prospect arrived sold, not because the process produced it — score the process accordingly.
